purpose: A separate fresh-phrasing faculty exercise. No expected grades or faculty judgments are encoded. Do not tune the engine to these examples before independent review.

turns: Lately, you have considered ending your own life.
Lately, have you considered ending your own life?

pairs.discussion: How do you describe the learner's conversational move in each version? Does the patient reply support the same or a different observation?

turns: During this week, have thoughts about suicide come up?
During this week, you haven't had thoughts about suicide, right?

pairs.discussion: Does the wording invite the same range of responses? Discuss the learner's move separately from the information in the actual patient reply.

turns: Since arriving here, have you wanted to kill yourself?
At handover I read, “Since arriving here, have you wanted to kill yourself?”

pairs.discussion: What supports your interpretation of who is being addressed? Distinguish reading a quoted question from directing a question to the patient; retain uncertainty if the exchange does not settle it.

before: Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?

turns: Have you made any plans to end your life?
Could you get to those pills?
What helps you choose to stay alive?
Have you made any plans to end your life? Could you get to those pills? What helps you choose to stay alive?

pairs.discussion: Which questions received relevant answers in each exchange? Compare the entire follow-up sequence, and separate wording the engine missed from information the patient did or did not provide.
